Compare several scenarios against one baseline, starting from layers

Source: R/compare-scenarios.R
habitat_connectivity_scenarios.Rd

Each layer in habitat_scenarios or barrier_scenarios is its own scenario that changes that one layer; the lists are never combined. A habitat scenario runs against barrier_baseline, and a barrier scenario against habitat_baseline. For a scenario that changes both layers, use habitat_connectivity_comparison().

Usage

habitat_connectivity_scenarios(
  habitat_baseline,
  barrier_baseline,
  species,
  interpatch_distance,
  habitat_scenarios = NULL,
  barrier_scenarios = NULL,
  directions = 4,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

habitat_baseline

Terra SpatRaster. The baseline habitat layer: the landscape as it is today.

barrier_baseline

Terra SpatRaster. The baseline barrier layer.

species

Species name. E.g., "Superb Fairy Wren".

interpatch_distance

Numeric. The distance (in metres) at which habitat patches are considered connected. May be a scalar or a vector; a vector runs every scenario once per distance.

habitat_scenarios

A named list of habitat layers, one per scenario. Names become the scenario_name column.

barrier_scenarios

A named list of barrier layers, the mirror of habitat_scenarios. Give either list, or both; names must be unique across the two.

directions

Which neighbouring raster cells join into one patch, passed to terra::patches(). 4, the default, is the rook's case: cells join only through a shared edge. 8 is the queen's case: cells that touch only at a corner join as well. It applies to rasters only, not to sf_habitat_connectivity().

verbose

Logical. Display progress messages (default: TRUE).

Value

A compare_connectivity object with four rows per scenario per distance, labelled in the scenario_name column. Habitat scenarios come first, then barrier scenarios, in the order given.

Details

The layer-level counterpart to compare_scenarios(): it runs the connectivity pipeline on each scenario and compares them all against the baseline. The baseline is run once per distance and reused by every scenario, so comparing three scenarios at one distance runs the pipeline four times, not six.

Each scenario layer must be the whole layer after the change, on the same grid as the layer it replaces, or this gives an error: put it there with onto_grid().

See also

compare_scenarios() when you already have connectivity objects, habitat_connectivity_comparison() for one scenario, including one that changes both layers, and vignette("scenario-comparison").

Examples

# \donttest{
wren_habitat <- example_wren_habitat()
wren_barrier <- example_wren_barrier()

habitat_connectivity_scenarios(
  habitat_baseline = wren_habitat,
  barrier_baseline = wren_barrier,
  species = "Superb Fairy Wren",
  interpatch_distance = 200,
  habitat_scenarios = list(
    "Bentley Project" = example_wren_habitat_scenario()
  ),
  barrier_scenarios = list(
    "Barrier upgrade" = example_wren_barrier_scenario()
  ),
  verbose = FALSE
)
